answers.headline: Executes nothing it drafts
answers.qualifier: one schema read grounds it, nothing else reaches the database
answers.title: Plan mode drafts, and never runs what it drafted
answers.body: Plan mode never executes the statement it wrote, on any engine — production included. Its one reach is the schema capture that grounds it: metadata only, no data rows, and it is where the inventory in Run details came from. On PostgreSQL and SQLite that capture is itself a catalog read; on every other engine it asks the provider to describe its own schema.

answers.headline: Cannot execute on BigQuery
answers.qualifier: plan mode drafts here, and the operations workflow still runs
answers.title: Agent mode has no read-only statement path on BigQuery
answers.body: Agent mode executes only where the provider implements a read-only statement path under a boundary it declares: PostgreSQL, SQLite, DuckDB, SQL Server, MySQL, Kubernetes, MongoDB, ClickHouse, libSQL, InfluxDB 3 (SQL), Elasticsearch, OpenSearch, Oracle, Db2 LUW, Apache Cassandra, Couchbase, Apache Druid, LibreDB, InfluxDB (InfluxQL), Weaviate, Qdrant, Neo4j, Milvus, Redis, etcd, Oxia, RabbitMQ, Apache Kafka, S3-compatible object storage, Firestore, SNMP, NETCONF, Modbus, Prometheus, OPC UA, MTConnect, MQTT, Sparkplug B and Trino. On BigQuery a run whose workflow sends a statement is refused when it is started, before a run is opened. The operations workflow still runs here, because it sends no statement at all: it takes the operational readings this engine offers agent mode. Plan mode drafts on every engine.

answers.headline: Reads only
answers.qualifier: 200 rows and 10 s per statement, enforced by the engine
answers.title: Agent mode reads, under a boundary the engine enforces

Writes and DDL are refused by the engine rather than by reading the statement. Nothing reaches your editor unless you tick the hand-over when the run opens.

answers.headline: Reads only, and one statement in your editor
answers.qualifier: 500 rows, no time limit, same read-only session
answers.title: Reads only, and one statement lands in your editor
answers.body: The run always produces its answer on its own read-only path, bounded to 200 rows and 10 seconds. Tick this and it will also put that statement in your editor and run it there — on the connection the run was opened on, at the editor's 500-row limit and with no time limit. It is the same database-enforced read-only session either way, so writes and DDL are refused by the engine rather than by reading the statement. Statements whose plan reads as expensive, or which the run measured as slow, are put in the editor without being run.

answers.qualifier: metadata only, 200 rows and 10 s per command, as an etcd user whose roles grant READ only

Before every command the server must answer that authentication is on and that the connection's user is not root, holds no root role, and holds READ permissions only, on no range that holds every key or a key under a Kubernetes storage prefix such as /registry/, read from its own roles, so a user that may write even one key range, or could tell which Kubernetes Secrets exist, is refused, and the count of every key is refused by the server; a call the roles do not govern, such as granting a lease, is stopped by the reader, which sends none. Studio's reader refuses every other command before anything is sent. Nothing reaches your editor.

Agent reads of one device never overlap, across every run on this server, and Studio waits one second after each before the next one dials, so the plant's own client can reach a device that serves one client at a time; one run sends at most 64 requests to Modbus devices. Studio's agent client builds only Read Coils, Read Discrete Inputs, Read Holding Registers, Read Input Registers and Read Device Identification, and every frame passes a check that refuses any other function code before it is sent, so it cannot write. answers.headline: Executes nothing it drafts
answers.qualifier: no topic is listed for it; opening the connection is a handshake that subscribes to nothing
answers.title: Plan mode plans, and never runs what it planned
answers.body: Plan mode writes its plan in prose and never subscribes to the broker. It drafts no read request, because an MQTT connection has no query console that runs one: agent mode alone sends the window and topic reads. MQTT has no command that lists topics, and topic names are withheld from agent mode, so no inventory grounds the plan: the topics it names are the ones the question names. Opening the connection is a handshake, a connect and a disconnect, which subscribes to nothing, so no topic, payload or $SYS reading is read.

answers.headline: Reads only
answers.qualifier: metadata only, one row per read, each read one 3-second window within 10 s, over an encoder that cannot write a publish or a will
answers.title: Agent mode counts what an MQTT broker delivers in a window, and never publishes
answers.body: Agent mode runs MQTT reads it wrote itself, each one JSON request: the window read listens to every topic (the filter #) for 3 seconds and answers totals only, the distinct topics seen, the messages, the retained messages and the payload bytes; the topic read listens to one topic the request names in full and answers whether a message was seen on it and how many, and of the last message seen on it its retained flag, the QoS it was delivered at, its payload size and when it arrived. Every answer states how long it listened, why it stopped and that a topic not seen in the window may still exist, since MQTT has no command that lists topics. No answer names a topic or carries a payload, a user property or a $SYS reading, and a read whose time budget of 10 s cannot hold a whole window is refused rather than shortened. Each read is a fresh session that keeps nothing. Studio's MQTT encoder writes five packets and no publish, its connect has no will, and every outbound byte is checked again before it leaves, so agent mode cannot publish, register a will, take a shared subscription or write a topic filter of its own. Nothing reaches your editor.

answers.headline: Executes nothing it drafts
answers.qualifier: the server's read endpoints ground it, and no PromQL it drafted is evaluated
answers.title: Plan mode drafts, and never runs what it drafted
answers.body: Plan mode never sends the PromQL it wrote. It is grounded on the server's own read endpoints, the metric names of the last hour and their label names, the rule groups and rules, and the scrape pools and targets, and that grounding is where the inventory in Run details came from. Studio reads the series' label sets to learn their label names and keeps the names alone; a target is named by its address without userinfo, and the server's flags are not read.

answers.headline: Reads only
answers.qualifier: 200 rows and 10 s per read, over a transport whose only POST is the instant query
answers.title: Agent mode reads Prometheus with PromQL, and never writes
answers.body: Agent mode runs PromQL reads it wrote itself, each one expression evaluated as an instant query at the server's now, the way the console runs it, and answers the samples and labels as the console renders them: a vector one row per series, a matrix one row per sample, bounded to 200 rows and 10 seconds each, the server's time-out set from that budget, and refused past them rather than cut. Its inventory names the metrics and their label names, the rule groups and rules, and the scrape pools and targets. Withheld are the server's command-line flags, which carry paths, addresses and local configuration, and every URL's userinfo, query string and fragment in a target, rule or alert answer and in the labels of a PromQL answer, where a scrape token or a password can sit; a target, and an instance label, is named by its address without userinfo. The projection goes by a value's shape, so two reads reach what the server stores: a label value a read rewrites with label_replace so that it no longer reads as a URL or an address is answered as the read wrote it, and a label matcher selects on the value the server stores, so a read can test a value the projection withholds. Studio's transport builds requests to its own read endpoints only, so no admin, remote-write, OTLP or lifecycle call can be sent. Nothing reaches your editor.

answers.headline: Executes nothing it drafts
answers.qualifier: no group, edge node or device is listed for it; opening the connection is a handshake that subscribes to nothing
answers.title: Plan mode plans, and never runs what it planned
answers.body: Plan mode writes its plan in prose and never subscribes to the broker. It drafts no read request: the editor's console request reads metric values, which agent mode never reads, and agent mode alone sends the window, group, edge node and device reads. Sparkplug has no command that lists edge nodes or devices, and their ids are withheld from agent mode, so no inventory grounds the plan: the ids it names are the ones the question names. Opening the connection is a handshake, a connect and a disconnect, which subscribes to nothing, so no id, metric or stored certificate is read.

answers.headline: Reads only
answers.qualifier: metadata only, one row per read, each read one 3-second window within 10 s, over an encoder that cannot write a publish, a command or a will
answers.title: Agent mode counts what a Sparkplug plant publishes in a window, and never publishes
answers.body: Agent mode runs Sparkplug reads it wrote itself, each one JSON request: the window read listens to the whole spBv1.0 namespace (or, when the connection names one group, that group alone) for 3 seconds and answers totals only, the distinct groups, edge nodes and devices seen, the birth, death and data messages by type, the metrics they carried and their payload bytes; the group, edge node and device reads listen to one object the request names in full and answer whether it was seen, its messages by type, its metric count, whether a birth or a death was seen and when its last message arrived. Every answer states how long it listened, why it stopped and that an edge node or device not seen in the window may still exist, since a birth certificate is published at QoS 0 and not retained, and no answer says a node is online or offline. No answer names a group, edge node, device or host application, or carries a metric name, a value or a stored certificate, and a read whose time budget of 10 s cannot hold a whole window is refused rather than shortened. Each read is a fresh session that keeps nothing. Studio's Sparkplug encoder writes five packets and no publish, and its connect has no will, so agent mode cannot publish, send a command or a rebirth request, take a host application's role, register a will or write a topic filter of its own. Nothing reaches your editor.
